scope: iPhone compact-height landscape calendar controls, Year/Month date selection, exact-task route, toolbar Add and relaunch; portrait Month/short-period regressions.
changes: Compact-height non-Day calendars keep their natural heights in an outer vertical scroll surface, with shared task rows rather than a nested task-panel scroll view. Portrait/iPad retain their existing layout.
Accessibility date/Year lists use a 220-point compact-height viewport. Existing period paging and collapse remain.

Landscape Add moves from the floating overlay to a plain 44x44 toolbar button, preserving selected-date capture. The same explicit toolbar target also applies to Day. No persistence, sync, widget contract or sibling dependency changes.
build: ios-phone-compact-calendar-build-v6.log succeeds; strict genuine Apple Development app/widget/runner signatures and dedicated Simulator identities verified in phone-compact-calendar/signing.json.
acceptanceScope: Six accepted case/device pairs cover nine workflows: three final landscape routes, two focused Add settings, and four portrait workflows (Month plus 3-day/5-day/Week). Final landscape v4 and focused Add use build v6. Portrait regression uses build v4; subsequent changes affect compact-height date viewport, toolbar Add and test driver, with regular-height Month/short-period rendering unchanged.
nativeAssertions: Actual landscape window after launch and relaunch. All twelve Year targets fully inside visible content; largest targets also fully inside their date-list viewport; target sizes >=44x44.

Largest Month first/last dates fully visible and selected; Today task opens after collapse; exact title, Cancel, toolbar Add >=44x44, Today-dated draft and normal relaunch retaining original open tasks.
System period menu is scrolled within its visible collection. Outer calendar scrolling uses its margin, while inner date lists are scrolled within their own viewport.
intermediateFailures: Original phone v1: all three orientation predicates fail, remaining 402x874 portrait. Original device preserved; cause unproven.
Fresh disposable phone rotates. Clean baseline v1 fails all three: largest menu above screen (y -101/-139), normal Year first row extends outside pager.
Compact native v1/v2: normal Year passes; largest tests fail on driver assumptions about visible system menu choices. Native hierarchy shows scrollable menu collection and offscreen Week item.

Compact native v3: all three date/task routes reach toolbar Add, then fail actual height 36 despite 44-point label frame. Plain button style plus outer 44-point frame resolves this; focused Add v1 and final full v4 pass.

findings: Complete first/last normal Year cards and largest month rows are visible when scrolled; floating Add no longer covers cards. Adjacent partial rows and native translucent chrome are expected scroll states.
The largest landscape Add draft shows title/keyboard but a partly hidden date-control area. Date value is asserted semantically; full composer-control readability/reachability is not accepted.
The exact task title and native Save/Cancel controls are visible. These captures do not establish every editor section or input journey.

remaining: Largest landscape composer controls and nested-scroll ergonomics
Landscape short-period/Day planner and normal Month journeys beyond prior evidence
